Problem statement
Sarawak's rural areas see peak school dropout rates at ages 14–16. Families value education, but its payoff isn't as clear or immediate as a child developing farm skills instead. While the state and country run multiple initiatives to make farming a legitimate, credentialed career path, these are only open to school leavers aged 17 and above, leaving no way to track or recognize the skills a child develops through labor before that age, making those years look wasted rather than productive.

Pitch
We're building a digital micro-credentialing platform that turns farm labor into recognized qualifications regardless of age, letting kids as young as 12 start earning verified, stackable credentials for real skills like nursery care, pest management, and basic agri-bookkeeping. It's for rural Sarawakian kids and their guardians, so those early working years aren't wasted, and for MPOB, TVET providers, and mills who currently have no way to verify the skills these young workers already have by the time they're old enough to formally enter the pipeline.
